sentiment.rationale: The document reports a headline EPS miss ($5.87 vs ~$6.96 consensus) and an operating margin shortfall (28% vs 31.5% guidance), both attributed to a one-time Brazil tax charge. However, underlying operations were strong: revenue grew 17% YoY, ad revenue is on track to more than double, and engagement hit record TV-time shares. Critically, no forward guidance was raised or lowered — management deferred full-year 2026 guidance to the January call and offered no 2026 ad revenue guidance. The net effect is a genuinely mixed read with no change in forward expectations, anchoring the score at 0.0.

summary.eps: $5.87 versus roughly $6.96 consensus, an optical miss attributable to the Brazil charge.
summary.guidance: No full-year 2026 guidance given, deferred to the January call. No 2026 advertising revenue guidance provided.
summary.margin: Operating margin 28%, down from 30% a year earlier and below the 31.5% guidance, driven by a $619M Brazil tax expense.
key_risks: The EPS/margin miss itself, even if one-time.
The Brazil Supreme Court ruled against Netflix 7–4 on the tax scope.
No 2026 numbers on the table yet, with the market asked to wait until January.
Intensifying live-sports competition (Apple F1, Paramount UFC).
WBD / Warner Bros. acquisition rumours in the background (regulatory and execution overhang).
key_opportunities: Best ad-sales quarter ever, on track to more than double ad revenue in 2025.
Record share of TV time in Q3 in both the US and the UK.
Canelo-Crawford fight drew 41M+ live viewers and ranked top 10 in 91 countries.
Approaching 1 billion people globally for programming, still only ~7% of addressable consumer-spend market and ~10% of TV time in its biggest markets.
